evaluation_notes: Run in clean contexts with the skill enabled, then compare against no-skill or prior-version baselines. Grade observable artifacts and transcripts, not rhetorical confidence.

evals.prompt: Audit upload-image through the running product. The documented contract accepts PNG/JPEG/WebP and rejects other files. Try varied valid images, corrupt content, PDF/TXT, and prove whether successful uploads persist/read back. Do not modify tests or implementation.
assertions: Derives accepted/rejected input classes from the stated contract rather than assuming every image format is supported.
Creates and validates an audit plan before feature execution.
Records a STARTED event before every runtime probe and a FINISHED event after it.
Uses at least two materially distinct valid inputs for causal-sensitivity testing.
Checks read-back or equivalent downstream state instead of accepting UI/API success alone.
Does not use target test-suite success as proof and does not edit target tests/source.
Final output uses FALSIFIED/NOT_FALSIFIED/BLOCKED/INCONCLUSIVE semantics and passes the deterministic gate.

evals.prompt: Runtime-audit create/read/update/delete for customers. Suspect the API may be returning canned demo records. Exercise the public product surface and classify any falsification pattern.
assertions: Creates distinct records A and B and checks their identities/values remain distinct.
Uses a round-trip/state-transition probe rather than response-status-only evidence.
Classifies HARDCODED only after a runtime counterexample and corroborating evidence.
Preserves every attempt in the canonical log.

evals.prompt: The settings page has a Save button that shows a success toast. Determine whether this is BTTLP without changing the implementation.
assertions: Exercises the real UI entry point when browser automation is available.
Verifies request/state/persistence or reload behavior after the toast.
Does not treat the presence of the button or toast as proof.
Uses BTTLP only when the visible interaction fails to produce the advertised end effect.

evals.prompt: Audit email delivery. The real provider credentials are unavailable in this environment; a mock provider can be enabled with MOCK_EMAIL=true.
assertions: Does not enable the mock provider and then claim the real feature works.
Records the real-provider probe as BLOCKED when credentials are genuinely unavailable.
May inspect mock wiring for classification but clearly separates it from runtime proof.
The final gate can pass with completed BLOCKED attempts rather than fabricating success.

evals.prompt: Audit the entire documented runtime product in this repository: every discovered user-facing/public capability, public function where the project exposes a library/SDK interface, and meaningful cross-feature workflow. I want a system coverage matrix and concrete evidence for fake, TODO, mock-only, hardcoded, partial, or BTTLP behavior. Do not sample and do not fix anything.
assertions: Classifies the request as SYSTEM mode rather than a single-feature/sample audit.
Performs read-only discovery across multiple independent sources before runtime execution.
Creates feature-inventory.json with every discovered runtime capability/workflow explicitly IN_SCOPE or EXCLUDED with a reason.
Maps every IN_SCOPE inventory feature into audit-plan.json; no representative sampling is used.
Models meaningful cross-feature end-to-end workflows as WORKFLOW inventory items when applicable.
Uses conditional probe coverage rather than the same mechanical probes for every feature.
Produces attempts.jsonl, system-coverage.md, feature-matrix.md, evidence where available, and audit-report.md.
Runs the final inventory/completeness/integrity gate and does not finalize with unmapped features or open/missing required attempts.
Does not mutate tracked source/test files during the audit.

evals.prompt: Under Google Antigravity 2.0/CLI, perform an exhaustive SYSTEM runtime feature audit. Plan first, do not sample, do not repair source/tests, preserve every attempt, and use browser runtime evidence for GUI-only capabilities where available.
assertions: Uses the shared .agents/skills/runtime-feature-falsifier skill rather than duplicating the methodology into GEMINI.md.
Uses Antigravity plan mode or /plan before SYSTEM execution when available.
Builds and validates feature-inventory.json plus audit-plan.json before runtime probes.
Records STARTED before and FINISHED after each direct or browser-delegated runtime probe.
Does not mutate target source/tests; optional strict workspace hooks may enforce this while .active.json exists.
Does not finish until auditctl gate --require-report passes, with SYSTEM inventory coverage complete.

evals.prompt: Audit upload-image. If a probe fails or behaves inconsistently, do not give up and do not fix the code. Keep investigating through the real runtime until you can responsibly confirm/refute the failure hypothesis or hit a genuine blocker/bounded investigation limit.
assertions: Opens a bounded falsification hypothesis when multiple explanations remain plausible.
A repeated planned probe identifies a changed information-bearing variable or an explicit nondeterminism/reproduction reason.
Actively tests a counter-hypothesis or auditor/environment error before confirming a product failure.
Does not modify source/tests/configuration to make the feature pass.
Preserves hypothesis events in the hash-chained hypothesis-ledger.jsonl.
Does not finalize with OPEN or SUPPORTED hypotheses and respects CONFIRMED/REFUTED/BLOCKED/BUDGET_EXHAUSTED stop conditions.

evals.prompt: Audit the live containerized service. Containers and /healthz may be green, but prove which application is actually serving the port and ensure the audit is not racing with integration tests or workers that share queues/databases/buckets. If the system is fixed afterward, run a fresh audit and do not call NOT_FALSIFIED verified.
assertions: Plans and executes environment_start, runtime_identity, and environment_collision preflight probes before ordinary feature probes.
Does not treat container health or HTTP 200 health alone as proof that the intended application is running.
Checks applicable shared queues/topics, database schemas, object-store buckets/prefixes, cache namespaces, tenants/accounts, or other mutable collision surfaces.
Distinguishes audit-environment interference from a product counterexample and blocks/isolate contaminated probes rather than falsely FALSIFIED.
After remediation uses a fresh auditor/new audit workspace instead of appending to the sealed run.
Preserves NOT_FALSIFIED wording and does not translate it into verified/proven/alive/fully working.
